label.en: Rain in the 2026 wheat harvest window so far (from September 1)

notes.en: GPM IMERG via NASA POWER ends on 2026-09-14 at access, so the IMERG block covers only September 1-14. The NASA GES DISC copies (Early, Late, Final) need an Earthdata login, which this pipeline does not use; the NASA POWER block is the only one that covers the window.

Ground check not possible yet: the ANA web service had no 2026 data for rain gauge 2853015 at access ('Sem dados para esta estação'), and the INMET A853 station service did not answer from the pipeline.
Current ENSO state: ONI ASO 2026 = +2.46 degC, operational phase el nino; the SON 2026 season that sets the phase of the past years is not complete yet.

Arithmetic on the reported Emater figures: 2,833 / 2,968 kg/ha is 4.5% lower and 763,121 / 1,166,163 ha is 34.6% lower, so most of the reported 37.48% production drop comes from the smaller planted area; the yield estimate was made mid-harvest.

text.en: Wheat, Rio Grande do Sul, 2026 crop re-estimate (data of the first half of October): 763,121 ha (34.56% less than the 1,166,163 ha of 2025, IBGE); projected yield 2,833 kg/ha against 2,968 kg/ha in 2025 (the bulletin says 5.55% less); production 2,161,922 t, 37.48% less than the 3,458,083 t of 2025 (IBGE). Excess moisture and low solar radiation in key phases lowered the yield potential and raised disease pressure (Fusarium head blight, 'giberela'; wheat blast, 'brusone'). Ijuí region: the cycle nears its end with reduced yield potential; in Ibirubá (Alto Jacuí) yield and quality expectations were revised down.

Wheat, Rio Grande do Sul: 76% of the area harvested by 12 November 2026. Episodes of intense rain interrupted the harvest; in part of the fields excess moisture, low light, frosts and diseases lowered the yield potential and the commercial quality, with test weight (PH) mostly below 78 kg/hl, the Type 1 reference. Ijuí region: 72% harvested; PH between 72 and 75 in Santa Bárbara do Sul.
